items.title: Abbey Lincoln — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Max Roach, who really was the A&R on that, and Nat Hinthoff produced it.

ctx.x: Julian had said that when you sang it, it wasn't difficult anymore, somehow it was so natural to you, and I was wondering how that happened. Was it -­

Because Roach would play it. You know what I mean? I heard him play all these rhythms. I remember Coleman Hawkins saying when we did "Driver Man" in five four time, he said to me, "You hear that, don't you?" I said, "Yeah." He didn't hear it. So, Max would accent the first one, but after listening to him, I was privy to that. I listened while he played songs and I think I have a good ear, too, you know. I had a hard time singing "In The Red," and after we got it on tape and Nat Hinthoff came, he thought we had…
